statement: The function returns a result vector r of length n - k + 1. For every i with 0 <= i <= n - k, let W_i = nums[i..i+k-1] be the contiguous subarray of length k. For each integer v, let c_i(v) be the number of indices j with 0 <= j < k and W_i[j] = v. Let D_i = {v | c_i(v) > 0}. Let t_i = min(x, |D_i|). Let S_i be the set of t_i values from D_i with the t_i largest pairs (c_i(v), v) under lexicographic order; explicitly, if |D_i| <= x then S_i = D_i, and otherwise S_i consists of the x values with largest c_i(v), breaking ties in favor of the largest v. Then r[i] = sum_{v in S_i} v * c_i(v).
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). 1 <= n <= 50; for every j with 0 <= j < n, 1 <= nums[j] <= 50; 1 <= x <= k <= n. Interpret k and x as mathematical integers.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, len(r) = len(nums) - k + 1.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). 1 <= n <= 50; for every j with 0 <= j < n, 1 <= nums[j] <= 50; 1 <= x <= k <= n.

statement: The function returns a result r (it does not fail, panic, or overflow) for every input satisfying the preconditions.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). 1 <= n <= 50; for every j with 0 <= j < n, 1 <= nums[j] <= 50; 1 <= x <= k <= n.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every i with 0 <= i <= n - k, r[i] <= sum_{j=0}^{k-1} nums[i+j].
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). 1 <= n <= 50; for every j with 0 <= j < n, 1 <= nums[j] <= 50; 1 <= x <= k <= n.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every i with 0 <= i <= n - k, if the number of distinct values in the subarray nums[i..i+k-1] is strictly greater than x, then r[i] < sum_{j=0}^{k-1} nums[i+j].
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). 1 <= n <= 50; for every j with 0 <= j < n, 1 <= nums[j] <= 50; 1 <= x <= k <= n.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every i with 0 <= i <= n - k, r[i] >= x * min_{0 <= j < k} nums[i+j].
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). 1 <= n <= 50; for every j with 0 <= j < n, 1 <= nums[j] <= 50; 1 <= x <= k <= n.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every i with 0 <= i <= n - k, if the subarray nums[i..i+k-1] has at most x distinct values, then r[i] = sum_{j=0}^{k-1} nums[i+j].
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). 1 <= n <= 50; for every j with 0 <= j < n, 1 <= nums[j] <= 50; 1 <= x <= k <= n.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, if x = 1, then for every i with 0 <= i <= n - k, let W_i = nums[i..i+k-1] and for each integer v let c_i(v) be its number of occurrences in W_i. Let v_i be the value with c_i(v_i) > 0 that is lexicographically maximal by the pair (c_i(v_i), v_i). Then r[i] = v_i * c_i(v_i).
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). 1 <= n <= 50; for every j with 0 <= j < n, 1 <= nums[j] <= 50; 1 <= x <= k <= n.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every i with 0 <= i <= n - k, if the k elements of nums[i..i+k-1] are pairwise distinct, then r[i] equals the sum of the x largest values among nums[i..i+k-1].
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). 1 <= n <= 50; for every j with 0 <= j < n, 1 <= nums[j] <= 50; 1 <= x <= k <= n.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every i and j with 0 <= i <= n - k and 0 <= j <= n - k, if the multisets of values in the subarrays nums[i..i+k-1] and nums[j..j+k-1] are equal (equivalently, every integer occurs the same number of times in both windows), then r[i] = r[j].
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). 1 <= n <= 50; for every j with 0 <= j < n, 1 <= nums[j] <= 50; 1 <= x <= k <= n.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every i with 0 <= i <= n - k, there exists a set S_i of distinct values occurring in nums[i..i+k-1] such that |S_i| = min(x, d_i), where d_i is the number of distinct values in that window, and r[i] = sum_{v in S_i} v * c_i(v), where c_i(v) is the number of occurrences of v in the window.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). 1 <= n <= 50; for every j with 0 <= j < n, 1 <= nums[j] <= 50; 1 <= x <= k <= n.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every i with 0 <= i <= n - k, let W_i = nums[i..i+k-1] and for each integer v let c_i(v) be its number of occurrences in W_i. Let v_i be a value with c_i(v_i) > 0 that is lexicographically maximal by the pair (c_i(v_i), v_i). Then r[i] >= v_i * c_i(v_i).
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). 1 <= n <= 50; for every j with 0 <= j < n, 1 <= nums[j] <= 50; 1 <= x <= k <= n.

statement: Let r1 be the result returned by find_x_sum(nums, k, x1) and r2 the result returned by find_x_sum(nums, k, x2). Whenever both calls return, len(r1) = len(r2) = n - k + 1 and for every i with 0 <= i <= n - k, r1[i] <= r2[i].
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). 1 <= n <= 50; for every j with 0 <= j < n, 1 <= nums[j] <= 50; 1 <= x1 <= x2 <= k <= n. Interpret k, x1, x2 as mathematical integers.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every i with 0 <= i <= n - k, let W_i = nums[i..i+k-1]. If all distinct values occurring in W_i have the same positive frequency f, then r[i] = f * (the sum of the min(x, d_i) largest values occurring in W_i), where d_i is the number of distinct values in W_i.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). 1 <= n <= 50; for every j with 0 <= j < n, 1 <= nums[j] <= 50; 1 <= x <= k <= n.
